recent_posts.title: Latte 3.1 new features for PHP templating
recent_posts.summary: Latte 3.1 introduces five practical improvements to the PHP templating engine. The `ScopedLoopVariables` feature prevents foreach loop variables from leaking into the outer scope, restoring original values after the loop ends. The `Dedent` feature automatically removes common indentation inside paired tags at compile time with no runtime cost. Three new filters are added: `|commas` joins arrays with natural language separators (e.g., 'apple, pear and plum'), `|column` extracts a single column from arrays of records, and `|limit` takes the first N elements from arrays, iterators, or strings while preserving keys. The existing `|slice` filter is also extended to support iterators and generators with lazy memory-efficient evaluation. Both engine features are enabled via `setFeature()` or Nette configuration.

recent_posts.title: The Case of the Blocked Pipe
recent_posts.summary: A deep investigation into why Nette Tester's parallel test execution performs dramatically worse on Windows (21.6 seconds) compared to Linux (3 seconds). The root cause is Windows' lack of non-blocking I/O support for anonymous pipes, causing the test runner to freeze when reading from empty pipes. Multiple solutions were attempted—stream_set_blocking(), stream_select(), file-based output, and delayed reading—but each introduced new problems like deadlocks when test output exceeded the 4KB pipe buffer. The only viable solution would require rewriting the entire system to use TCP sockets instead of pipes.

recent_posts.title: Latte 3.1 brings smart HTML attributes and type safety to PHP templating
recent_posts.summary: Latte 3.1 introduces Smart HTML Attributes that understand context and data types, eliminating unnecessary conditions in templates. The update brings native mapping of PHP types to HTML attributes where null removes attributes entirely, booleans control attribute presence, and arrays serialize automatically for class/style/data attributes. It includes runtime type checking to catch errors during development, enables strict types by default, and adds a nullsafe filter operator (?|) for handling null values gracefully. The release also introduces syntactic improvements like n:elseif and provides a migration mode to safely upgrade from version 3.0.

recent_posts.title: Nette Tester 2.5.6 introduces HttpAssert for automated HTTP testing
recent_posts.summary: Nette Tester 2.5.6 introduces HttpAssert, a new class that simplifies automated HTTP testing for web applications. The tool allows developers to verify status codes, headers, response content, and handle redirects through a fluent API. It supports callback functions for advanced validation, flexible request configuration for all HTTP methods, and provides clear error messages when tests fail. The release also includes support for the upcoming PHP 8.5.

recent_posts.title: {linkBase} brings consistency to linking
recent_posts.summary: Nette Application 3.2.7 introduces the {linkBase} tag to solve linking consistency issues in shared templates across different presenter directory levels. The new tag allows relative links to be derived from a specified base module rather than the current presenter, eliminating broken links when layouts are reused. The update also includes an |absoluteUrl filter for normalizing URLs to absolute form.

recent_posts.title: Nette Assets: Finally unified API for everything from images to Vite – Nette Blog
recent_posts.summary: Nette Assets is a new library that unifies static file management in Nette PHP applications. It automatically handles image dimensions, cache busting through versioning, and provides native Vite integration with Hot Module Replacement. The library requires minimal configuration and offers custom mappers for various use cases like product image resizing and automatic Open Graph image generation. Key features include automatic URL construction, lazy loading of metadata, and support for multiple asset categories with fallback mechanisms.

recent_posts.title: Architecture That Grows with Your Project
recent_posts.summary: Proper code organization is a common challenge in PHP application development, and Nette documentation provides a comprehensive guide to directory structure. It discusses the benefits of a domain-oriented structure, making it easier to understand an application's purpose at a glance. The guide also offers principles to help evolve the structure as projects grow, making it useful for both new and existing projects.

recent_posts.title: Speed up your Nette application with lazy objects
recent_posts.summary: Lazy objects in PHP 8.4 and Nette 3.2.4 allow services to delay their initialization until they're actually used, speeding up application startup and reducing memory consumption. Enable this feature with just one line in the configuration. Lazy objects optimize your Nette applications without changing your existing code, but they only work with custom classes and require PHP 8.4 or higher.

recent_posts.title: Write Safer Code with the New Nette Database Documentation
recent_posts.summary: Nette Database now offers completely rewritten documentation that details its functionality and emphasizes database security. The documentation is available in 16 languages and is divided into sections based on whether developers prefer direct SQL queries or automated approaches. It includes numerous examples, practical use cases, and a thorough discussion of security risks, making it easier for developers to write safe and efficient code.

recent_posts.title: Nette Utils: Performance and Efficiency Generators
recent_posts.summary: The Nette Framework enhances efficiency by utilizing generators to improve performance and optimize memory usage. Key features include the `FileSystem::readLines()` method for reading large files incrementally, `Strings::matchAll()` with a lazy parameter for gradual regular expression matching, and the Iterables class for lazy evaluation of iterable structures. These innovations allow handling large data sets more elegantly without changing the code structure.
